shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a fixed 146,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine, with snow, altitude weather and windier peaks. Coast, river and lake tiles supported; Dubs Mint Minimap and Map Preview both patched.
body:
# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~68 files, ~18,300 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text; keep it that way.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather and settings passes are all VERIFIED IN PLAY. **Seven-level maps with a real basement now generate clean in 5.5 s (run #196).** Below-snow rendering is fixed but UNVERIFIED IN PLAY.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, with a permanently-fogged gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)*64`; **64-alignment is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position). Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** The path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted, and that bug class cannot appear on an ordinary square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river and lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a) | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b, §15d) | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
| Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims | water surface (§6b-LAKE) | none, cosmetic, accepted |
| **Map-wide scalar**, one per-tick value for the whole map | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16) | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

Classify a new bug into one of these six, but PROVE it. Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 146,000 cells, FIXED
`4 x 190 = 145,920` sets the figure. `5 x 190` and `3 x 254` are refused. `ABMapSizeLimit` owns it. **`7 x 126 = 112,896` is VERIFIED IN PLAY (run #196).**
Per-level size is SQUARE, which is why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` (it squares `Size.x`, not `map.Area`) already yields a per-BAND count. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`.

**⚠ The level chooser is also the lab.** `0 above / 0 below` generates an ORDINARY single-level map, the vanilla control. **STILL UNVERIFIED: does `0 up / 0 down` actually reach generation?** Pre-flight check: the strip must read 1 level and 36,100 cells.

**⚠ The chooser UI: own the widget, do not patch the data.** `Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play. Now our own radio buttons write `mapSize` directly. Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix.
**The level spinners are NOT known to be broken.** A `3 up / 0 down` map generated when `0 up / 3 down` was intended in run #190; that was USER ERROR, confirmed. Do not re-open without new evidence. **The plan PERSISTS between colonies**, so an untouched chooser silently reuses the last layout, which is the likeliest explanation for any "wrong plan" report.

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop routing STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
`RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof, because only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix normalises `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated drop. TEN systems share it. **Seven separate appearances of the single `- Slot` bug**; grep every `- Slot` before trusting new code.
Sun-shadow subtlety: its mask is neighbour-based, so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the smallest drop among the nine cells.
Still single-band: the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Four rejected attempts on record: force-linked wall masks, high-queue cover, wall-sprite suppression, and theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Check for ground before diagnosing anything about the top level. Independently confirmed by timing in §9e.
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS A SET OF MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` is a faithful port of vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Every OTHER vanilla pass that contributes to how ground looks needs its own mirror, or that contribution is simply absent from the below view. Confirmed twice:
- **Water** (§6b): `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen`.
- **Snow** (§6f): `SectionLayer_ABBelowSnow`.
Before adding a below-view feature, ask which vanilla SectionLayer draws it. Existing mirrors: BelowV2 (terrain + things + fog fan), BelowLighting, BelowShadows, BelowWatergen, BelowSnow, MountainCap.
**Cross-band invalidation is already solved and is flag-agnostic:** `Patch_MapDrawer_ABMirrorDirtyUp` mirrors every dirty flag verbatim to EVERY band above (one step was not enough once levels stacked; symptom was "ground floor mineables disappear on floor 2"). So a new mirrored layer costs one `relevantChangeTypes` line, not a new propagation path.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: 1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
`SectionLayer_Watergen` (vanilla, `internal`, cannot be subclassed) is `SectionLayer_Terrain` plus `waterDepthMaterial`, drawn to the WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's layer. The visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that texture at its own SCREEN position.
- Water missing from upper levels, FIXED: `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
- Rivers not generating, FIXED: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately). `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first.

# 6b-LAKE. CLOSED: surface streaking accepted as vanilla appearance
PROVEN in run #173: a tile with water but no water mutators still streaked. **The ghost-river theory is dead; do not revive it.** Found en route: vanilla's flow builder ends `zero /= (float)num3` with no zero guard, writing NaN into a bilinear-filtered texture.

# 6c, 6d, 6e. COMPAT AND COASTS (all verified)
**Dubs Mint Minimap:** ONE RECT, not seven patches. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. Reflection only.
**Map Preview:** never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`. Generate at full stacked height and crop via `TexCoords`. `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500, a stack reaches 896).
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`, NO SCALING. Nine coastal mutators, none override `GetNoiseValue`.

# 6f. BELOW-SNOW (`SectionLayer_ABBelowSnow.cs`, UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
Snow lying on a lower level was invisible from above. Not masking, not translation, not the descent rule: **no mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed**, so below-snow was never emitted.
**The near-miss that hid it:** `CellTerrainAt` genuinely samples `map.snowGrid.GetDepth(below)` from the correct cell, but `CellTerrain`'s snow coverage is consumed only by `MaterialFor` to pick the POLLUTED terrain variant. The right value was read for an entirely different purpose, which is the kind of thing that survives review.
**Why it was simpler than the terrain mirror:** vanilla's snow layer emits no per-cell geometry. It builds ONE solid 9-verts-per-cell grid over the section and writes only vertex COLOURS, depth in alpha. That grid is positional and our section already sits in the viewing band, so nothing needs translating; only the sampled cells move. No vertex fix-up, no `- Slot`.
Details: geometry built once and reused (NOT `ClearSubMeshes(All)`, unlike every other AB layer, or colour count stops matching vertex count); iteration order must match `MakeBaseGeometry` (x outer, z inner, nine per cell); cells with nothing below still emit nine transparent vertices or all later colours shift; altitude matches the below-terrain print (`TerrainScatter`) to reproduce vanilla's own terrain/snow relationship; all nine kernel samples taken at the CENTRE cell's drop, because mixing two bands into one smoothing kernel would seam.
**⚠ Open risk:** draw ordering is queue-decided, not altitude-decided. `MatBases.Snow` may need queue work to sit above below-terrain and under below-things. Expect one iteration, as water did.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1 + 0.45*(depth-1))`, cave openness `x(1 + 0.35*(depth-1))`, both applied AFTER the settings clamp.
**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.** `SteadyEnvironmentEffectsTick` computes `outdoorMeltAmount` once per tick for the whole map and never calls `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. Dead for months behind a confident, wrong sentence.
**Climate defaults** (per colony, §17): +1 = -7, +2 = -16, +3 = -35, basement flat -6, wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50. **No ceiling clamp by design.**

# 8. CAMERA
`ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by LEVEL, not band index. `maxZoom` left DERIVED. `panMargin` 63.5 on every level. `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED.

# 9. GENERATION COST: DIAGNOSED AND LARGELY FIXED (runs #188, #190, #196)

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
`ABGenProfile.Report` prints `TILE` (id, biome, hilliness, elevation, temp, rainfall, coastal, mutators), `PLAN` (bands, height, surface band, up/down, doomed cells), a `SCOPING:` toggle line, and two censuses (`DESTROYED by def`, `SUPPRESSED by def`). Added because four earlier carve timings lacked the tile and are uninterpretable. It caught a changed tile on its FIRST use and voided a comparison that would otherwise have been believed.

## 9b. ⚠ THE COST IS DESTRUCTION, NOT GENERATION
Run #188, tile 846, TemperateForest/Mountainous/Mountain+Caves, 190x768, 4 bands:
| Phase | ms |
|---|---|
| All 42 gensteps (wall) | 3,972 |
| AB band carve | **20,447** |
| of which `Sky clear` | **20,126** (98.4%) |
| `Map.FinalizeInit` | 169 |
| things destroyed | 74,584 |

Generation is 16%, destruction 84%. **The original "scoping saves both halves" framing was WRONG.** Per-destroy price is 0.19 to 0.27 ms and STABLE across runs and tiles, so **op count is the only lever**. Mechanism is `ListerThings` removal, a linear `List.Remove` over ~100k-item lists, hence superlinear savings.
**CLOSED:** carving before `FinalizeInit` is worth at most 169 ms of 24,600.

## 9c. The culprit was rock, proven by census
Run #190: `SUPPRESSED` 43,517 rock vs `DESTROYED` 4,939 total of which only 238 rock. Rock moved columns, 99.5% of it. Would-be total 48,456, so **rock was 90% of everything the carve deleted**.

## 9d. SHIPPED: `ABDoomedBands.cs`
Suppresses `GenSpawn.Spawn(ThingDef,...)` inside `GenStep_RocksFromGrid` for doomed SKY band cells. Safe because: **shape** (per-cell noise test, no count redistributed, same licence as the plant skip); **state-neutrality** (only the spawn is cancelled, roofs / roof cleanup / `ScatterLumpsMineable` all still run, and `ClearCellHard` never touched roofs, so `ABSkyBandGen` gets bit-identical state); **sky only**. Patched on the `ThingDef` overload so the cancel precedes `ThingMaker.MakeThing`.

## 9e. Run #196: the first basement, and the bottleneck moved
Tile 54863, Desert/Mountainous/Mountain+Caves, 126x896, **7 bands, surface band 3, 3 up / 3 down**. Gensteps 2,289 ms, carve 3,180 ms, total ~5.5 s for SEVEN levels.
```
FillRock  bands 0,1,2   827.7 + 933.3 + 845.4 = 2,606 ms  (82% of carve)
Sky clear bands 4,5,6   168.6 + 120.0 +  12.4 =   301 ms  ( 9%)
```
**The sky side is solved.** The basement is now the whole cost.
**⚠ MY OWN §9d CAUTION IS FALSIFIED.** I argued against suppressing vanilla rock in basement bands because `FillRock` keeps it. Run #196 gives the hit rate for the first time: 47,628 basement cells, 40,755 fresh spawns, so **the keep hits only 6,873 times (14.4%)** (vanilla only places rock where elevation > 0.7, and the def must match too). Rock destroyed in the basement: 5,309 Granite + 1,804 Slate = **7,113**. Suppressing there trades 7,113 destroys (~1.4 s) for 6,873 extra spawns (~200 ms), because destroys cost roughly 7x spawns inside the generation window. **Net ~1.2 s, about 38% of the remaining carve.** The shape of the reasoning was right; the magnitude was never checked, because no basement had ever run.
**Sign flip, a confirmation not a bug:** with rock suppressed, `Sky clear` per band INVERTED (125/415/528 rising) versus #188 (7517/7029/5580 falling). Rock tapers upward (§6), so higher bands have more OPEN ground, and chunks/rubble only grow on open ground.
**⚠ `CavernGen` read 0.9 / 0.0 / 0.0 ms** on a tile carrying the Caves mutator. Either the basement genuinely has no cave systems or openness is at zero. UNDIAGNOSED.
**FALSIFIED, still dead:** "band 1 is consistently ~3x bands 2-3."
**Do not blanket-skip** water or coast mutators; §6b, §6e, §6d depend on them.

## 9f. Next targets, ranked
1. **Basement rock suppression** (§9e), ~1.2 s, the largest remaining item.
2. **`GenStep_RockChunks`**, 88% of what survives on sky-only maps (`Filth_RubbleRock` 3,183 + chunks 1,183 of 4,939). Verified per-cell probabilistic, passes the shape test. ~0.9 s.
3. **Scattered ruins, also a CONTENT BUG.** Deleted from doomed bands: `Wall`, `AncientFence`, `AncientGiantWheel`, `Filth_MachineBits`, `Steel`. Per §2 a scatterer's count is sized for ONE band but placement spans the whole stack, so **the surface is losing a large share of the ruins vanilla intended**. Fixes content and cost together. ⚠ Paired risk: run #190 logged `AncientExostriderRemains could not find cell to generate at`, the §15b starvation signal, so the derived seam margin must be re-checked at the same time.

# 10, 11. PERF AND LINKS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns, mod approximately 2% of frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry. Elevator SHIPPED but untested.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
Band info, below layer and pawn reports, water report, transit health, stuck probe, lighting/shader/biome reports, bisect toggles, ABGenProfile, camera calibration.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST in the pinned palette across runs.** Run #172 opened with a stale `belowWater=False` that mimicked a fixed bug exactly. Scoping toggles are now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE for this reason.
**⚠ Poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts.** Single-occurrence `[RimWorld]` warnings are filtered from summaries. Confirmed again in #190: a scatterer starvation warning and a `DropThingsNear` failure surfaced only via `monitor_poll`.
**⚠ The auto-prompt is edge-triggered per run.** A second occurrence of the same log call site never re-prompts; use `monitor_get_error` (returns the LATEST occurrence) or watch the `×count`.
`AB2: band info` is the fastest ground truth for "what did this map actually generate as"; it settled a level-plan question in one line after three messages of theorising.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **Verify below-snow in play** (§6f). Needs a snowy or cold tile with a populated level beneath the viewing level. Queue ordering is the expected failure mode.
2. **Basement rock suppression** (§9e/9f), ~38% of the remaining carve.
3. **`CavernGen` did nothing in the basement** (§9e). Three levels of solid rock with no caves is plausible but unconfirmed.
4. **⚠ A banded generation produced NO profile at all.** The 126x512 map in run #190 generated as banded yet `ABGenProfile.Report` never emitted, though the same call site fired earlier in the run. `Report` is unconditional and no error appeared. Unexplained.
5. **Unexplained in #190:** `DropThingsNear ... near (59, 0, 476)` on a map whose start spot was `(63, 0, 63)`. Possibly benign (that surface generated as solid rock).
6. §9f item 3 (ruins content deficit).
7. **Audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators**: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley.
8. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, reload fix. Basement GENERATION now verified (#196); basement PATHING and wormholes still are not.
9. Realtime-things pass still single-band. Selection bracket drifts upward as you zoom out. Waterfalls, combat never verified, vertical conduit, **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. A documented rejection may be re-opened only by naming the confound that invalidated it. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. An exact number is a diagnosis. Use the product's own knobs as lab equipment. A beautiful fit is not evidence. Knowing when to stop is a result.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed.** Generation was 16%, deletion 84%. The fix was right, the reason was wrong, and only the profile said so.
**⚠ A census beats a magnitude.** "74,584 things" is not a diagnosis; "43,517 Granite and Limestone" is. Pair a SUPPRESSED census with a DESTROYED one so the two are a conservation check, and the saving can be computed from ONE run without a matched A/B.
**⚠ Stamp the experiment's conditions into its own output.** The tile stamp voided a bad comparison on its first run.
**⚠ Evidence consistent with both hypotheses is not evidence.** "The size selection stuck, so the spinners must be broken" was wrong: an untouched spinner reusing a persisted value looks identical. Ask what a datum looks like under the OTHER hypothesis before spending it.
**⚠ An optimisation you declined for a stated reason still owes you the number.** The basement keep was left alone on the reasoning that it saved work; when a basement finally ran, the hit rate was 14.4% and the decision inverted. A conservative choice is still a claim.
**⚠ When a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes.** Twice now: water (two passes, screen-space) and snow (its own SectionLayer). A below view that mirrors one vanilla layer mirrors only that layer.
**⚠ A correct value read for the wrong purpose looks like coverage.** Below-snow was sampled correctly and used only to pick a pollution variant. Grep for the value's CONSUMER, not just its read site.
**Claims versus facts.** A comment asserting why something is safe to delete is a claim (§7). Re-measure the assumption you are about to build on. Verify a patched branch is reachable before debugging your own logic.
**Shapes.** Classify into one of the six. A slice of a tall map is not a short map. A uniform symptom is a scale or constant, a patchy one is data. An odd/even symptom is arithmetic.
**Patching.** When N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through. Patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it. Patch the idempotent READ, not the cached WRITE. Own the widget instead of patching the data it reads. Never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature. **Suppress the callee, not the caller**, when a genstep does several jobs and only one is waste.
**Engine facts.** `TerrainDef.holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Draw order inside and across SectionLayers is settled by material render QUEUE, not by altitude. Altitude is draw order for things, and `WorldClipper` sorts above `Skyfaller`. A null global texture falls back to the shader's default. Vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero. A spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter. `Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation, so generation-time patches must read the pending layout. `SectionLayer` subclasses are auto-discovered by `Section`'s constructor. Any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. Statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak; use a CWT. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED, which is why the same work costs ~40x after `FinalizeInit`.**

---

# 15. QOL PASS (verified, run #172)
**15a. Nothing may exist in the void.** `ABBandSafety.cs`. Finders answer inside the surface band; a prefix on the 7-arg `GenSpawn.Spawn` rewrites `loc`; a 120-tick sweep catches teleports and pre-fix saves. Always relocates to the SURFACE. Scoped to pawns and the gutter only.
**15b. Structures must not straddle a seam.** `GenGrid.CloseToEdge` measured against `map.Size`, so the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere. One prefix re-bases onto the cell's own band rect; eleven cold call sites inherit it. Backstop: postfix on `GenStep_Scatterer.CanScatterAt`. Seam margin DERIVED (`bandHeight/24`, clamped 4 to 12); a flat 10 starved scatterers on small bands.
**15c.** `panMargin` 63.5 on every level.
**15d. Vanilla's no-build map edge REMOVED on banded maps.** Per-band is one flag away. Consequence: vanilla's strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge.
**15e. Drop pods fall through the levels.** Suppress `Skyfaller.DrawAt`, re-issue via `DrawNowAt` translated by `(viewedBand - itsBand) * Slot`. Altitude chosen PER FRAME. `Skyfaller_FlyingPawn` excluded.

# 16. ALTITUDE AND WEATHER (`ABBandWeather.cs`, verified)
One weather INTERPRETED per band, since `WeatherManager` is per-Map.
- **Snow confined to real ground:** `AB_OpenAir` and `AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`.
- **Melt per band:** prefix on `DoCellSteadyEffects` rewrites the private `outdoorMeltAmount` on EVERY call including level 0.
- **Snow must exist before it can persist:** `SeedAltitudeSnow` at generation, seeded from CURRENT temperature. ~18 ms, free.
- **Rain falls and draws as snow above the line.** Accumulation via the public `AddFallenSnowAt`; vanilla gates on the cached field but takes the amount from the live property. Rejected: swapping `WeatherDef.Worker.overlays`, a global Def shared across maps.
- **No overlays underground**, judged on the viewed band.
- **Wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50, zero underground.** Patched on the `DesiredPowerOutput` getter. `CalculateWindCells` spans 22 rows, gutter is 2.
- **Readout:** `GlobalControls.TemperatureString` rebuilt from `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. `MapTemperature.OutdoorTemp` is NEVER reached by it, because outdoor cells still belong to a Room and `Room.Temperature` is a stored field.
- **Rendering:** snow on a level below needs its own mirrored pass, §6f.

# 17. SETTINGS PASS (verified)
**Tabbed scrolling window:** Performance, Climate, Sky, Basement, Diagnostics. Hand-drawn tab buttons, not `TabDrawer`. Each tab draws inside a try/catch that renders the exception into the pane.
**⚠ The blank-tab bug.** Scroll-view content height measured from the previous frame's `list.CurHeight` is a SELF-SUSTAINING LATCH without a floor. Fix: `Mathf.Max(list.CurHeight + 16f, inner.height)`. Diagnosed by one label drawn OUTSIDE the scroll view.
**⚠ Draw the diagnostic OUTSIDE the thing being diagnosed.** A fallback error rendered inside a clipped region is silent, and its silence is not evidence.
**The unlock gate.** The checkbox writes to a LOCAL; `unclampMapSize` only becomes true inside the confirmation callback, so the stored value IS the record that the warning was read. Red banner reports the multiple over budget, coloured against the BUDGET, not `Fits()`.
**The budget stays a `const`**, deliberately.
**Climate SNAPSHOTTED onto `ABBandMap` at generation** (`SnapshotClimate`, scribed, on BOTH carve paths). Order: snapshot, settings, hardcoded defaults.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`, `quicktest=false` (the level chooser needs the menus; Map Preview doubly so).
Compat tests need the target mod as a companion. Dubs (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`), Map Preview (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) and VQE Ancients (`vanillaquestsexpanded.ancients`) are all INACTIVE in the user's real list. **VQE Ancients co-loaded clean in run #196, but added no gensteps and no census entries, so its colony-map surface was barely exercised; its content is likely quest-site based. `ScenParts` rose from 15.8 ms to 332.2 ms, the only sign it ran.**
Water tests need a river or lake tile, coastline tests a coastal one. **Read the TILE line before comparing two runs.**
**Re-check the level strip before generating.** The plan persists between colonies.
Read the bisect line before trusting any water or snow observation.
